lesson.title: Area and Perimeter
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 5, Session 1
lesson.footer: Area and Perimeter | Year 5/6 Maths | Session 1

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Measurement, Years 5-6: solving practical problems with the perimeter and area of rectangles and shapes made of rectangles, using length x width; supported by Number VC2M5N06 and VC2M5N07 (efficient multiplication and division) and checking that answers are reasonable
plan.shape: three short model-then-try cycles (perimeter with missing sides, area by splitting the long side, then the same L-shape's area), because each new step is short and the contrast between edge and inside is the point
plan.criticalFeature: perimeter adds every side once and is measured in metres; area multiplies length by width and is measured in square metres
decisionPoints: the choice check: which answer is the area of a 6 m by 4 m garden
the hinge: area of an L-shape
the exit ticket: perimeter and area of the pool
plan.anchor: perimeter goes around the edge (add the sides); area covers the inside (length x width)

manipulatives: Square tiles or grid paper for counting (optional)
studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The anchor on the board: perimeter goes around the edge (add the sides); area covers the inside (length x width)
Under it: split a big shape into rectangles

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Perimeters and areas of rectangles, L-shapes for edge and inside, and fence, court and garden problems, with a mistake to fix.

example.prompt: Find the perimeter and the area of a rectangle 16 m by 5 m.

items.prompt: Find the perimeter and the area of each rectangle.

example.prompt: Find the perimeter and the area of this L-shape.

Find the missing sides, the perimeter and the area.

example.prompt: A pen is 20 m by 15 m. Fencing costs $10 a metre. Cost?
steps: Fence goes around the edge: (20 + 15) × 2 = 70 m.

items.prompt: A paddock is 45 m by 28 m. Fencing costs $12 a metre. How much does it cost to fence?
A netball court is 30 m by 15 m. How much ground does it cover?
Jai found the area of a 12 m by 5 m garden. Find his mistake and fix it.
items.answer: He found the perimeter. Area = 12 × 5 = 60 m².

items.prompt: A vegetable patch covers 96 m². One side is 8 m. How long is the other side?

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. The same fence making different spaces, working backwards from an area, and a path around a pool, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Edge and Inside Puzzles
resources.subtitle: Perimeter goes around the edge (add the sides). Area covers the inside (length x width).

example.prompt: 20 m of fence. Which rectangle pens can you make with whole metres?
steps: Every pen has a perimeter of 20 m.

items.prompt: A farmer has 24 m of fencing for a rectangular pen. Fill in the table. Which pen gives the most space inside?
Now you have 30 m of fence. Which whole-metre pen gives the most space inside? What do you notice about the best pens?
items.answer: Length + width = 15. 8 m by 7 m gives 56 m², the most. The closer the pen is to a square, the more space inside.

example.prompt: A rectangle has area 48 m² and one side 6 m. Perimeter?

items.prompt: A rectangle has area 91 m² and one side 7 m. What is its perimeter?
A square has an area of 81 cm². What is its perimeter? How do you know?
items.answer: 9 × 9 = 81, so each side is 9 cm. Perimeter 36 cm.

example.prompt: A 10 m by 8 m lawn has a 4 m by 3 m garden bed in it. Lawn area?

items.prompt: A pool is 12 m by 6 m. A path 1 m wide goes all the way around it. What is the area of the path?
items.answer: Pool and path: 14 × 8 = 112 m². Pool: 12 × 6 = 72 m². Path: 112 - 72 = 40 m².

example.prompt: Perimeter of a 5 cm by 2 cm rectangle?

items.hint: The two sides you cannot see match the ones you can.

items.hint: Count one row, then how many rows.
Count the rows going up first.

slides.notes: Area and perimeter in one session: around the edge, then the inside, then shapes made of rectangles.

Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk and write the anchor on the board. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet. Behind time? Skip the 4-digit fluency and the fourth We Do item.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with some chance and some angles.
ASK: What is the probability of blue?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 2/6. ACCEPT: 1/3
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> count every equal part, then the blue parts. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Blue is 2 of the 6 equal parts,
so 2/6, which is 1/3. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 2/4, blue parts over the other parts.
Fix: the bottom number counts every part, and they recount.
notes.prep: Review of Week 4 probability, kept from the original Week 5 decks. Two review items only today: under 4 minutes.

beats: ASK: How big is the reflex angle?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 280
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> trace the full turn, then take away the inside angle. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 280 degrees, because 360 take away 80 is 280.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 100, from 180.
Fix: trace all the way round, and they redo it from 360.
notes.prep: Week 1 review: reflex angles, spaced four weeks back.

slides.title: Multiply with the written method: 3 digits

beats: SAY: Now for some written multiplication.
Multiply the ones first, and carry into the next column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 2 082
SCAN boards for the carried digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 2 082.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: forgetting to add the carried digit after multiplying.
Fix: write each carry small above the next column, and they redo it.
notes.prep: Multiplication fluency feeds today's areas: 3 digits, then 4. Keep the block under 4 minutes.

slides.title: Multiply with the written method: 4 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 4 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 11 424
SCAN boards for the carried digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 11 424.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: forgetting to add the carried digit after multiplying.
Fix: write each carry small above the next column, and they redo it.
notes.prep: One size up, then straight to the LI.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to find the perimeter and area of rectangles and shapes made of rectangles.
successCriteria: I can find the perimeter by adding every side once.
I can find the area of a rectangle by multiplying length by width.
I can find the area of an L-shape by splitting it into rectangles.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Today is all about two measures:
the distance around a shape, and the space inside it.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 perimeter is reachable for everyone; SC2 area of a rectangle is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 composite area is the stretch.

slides.title: Edge or inside?
slides.prompt: How far around the edge? How many squares cover the inside?

beats: POINT to the edge, then the squares.
SAY: This garden has a fence around it and squares of lawn inside.
ASK: Write two numbers: how far around, and how many squares inside.
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 20 and 21
SCAN boards for 20 and 21.
80%+ -> cold call one student: How did you get 21 so fast?
Less -> trace the edge together, then count one row and the rows. Re-ask.
SAY: Around the edge: 7 and 3 is 10, doubled is 20 metres.
Inside: 3 rows of 7, 21 squares. Two numbers, two different measures.
trap: counting the squares along the edge for the distance.
Fix: trace the fence line, not the squares, and they add the sides.
notes.prep: Re-grounds both ideas from a picture anyone can count, so no one needs last week. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: The total distance around the outside of a shape.
slides.example: A 3 m by 2 m rug has a perimeter of 10 m.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is perimeter. Say it with me: pe-rim-e-ter.
SAY: Perimeter goes around the edge, so we add the sides.
Every side, once.
ASK: Trace the perimeter of your desk with your finger.
5 sec. Cue: Voices off. Trace... now.
EXPECT: fingers moving around the edge
trap: rubbing the middle of the desk.
Fix: say edge, not inside, and they trace again.
notes.prep: First half of the anchor. Brisk: under 2 minutes.

slides.meaning: The amount of surface a shape covers, measured in square units.
slides.example: A 5 m by 3 m rug covers 15 square metres, written 15 m².

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is area. Say it with me: ar-e-a.
SAY: Area covers the inside, so we multiply length by width.
We measure it in squares, like square metres, written m with a little 2.
ASK: Show me with your hand: is area the edge or the inside?
5 sec. Cue: Voices off. Show me... now. Hold it.
EXPECT: hands rubbing the inside of the desk
trap: writing m instead of m².
Fix: point to the squares, and they add the little 2.
notes.prep: Second half of the anchor. The unit tells you which one you found: m or m².

slides.title: Perimeter: find the missing sides
steps: Your turn: a 10 cm by 9 cm rectangle.

beats: SAY: Perimeter goes around the edge, so I add the sides.
Bottom 10, top 6, so the missing across side is 4.
ASK: Left is 9, right part is 4. Missing up side?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 5
MODEL adding all six, clicking in each step: 38. Every side, once.
ASK: What is the perimeter of a 10 by 9 rectangle?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 38 cm
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
Cold call one student: Why is it the same as the L-shape?
trap: leaving out the missing sides.
Fix: count the sides, six, and they add them all.
notes.stretch: Does cutting a different corner change the perimeter?
notes.help: Tick each side as you add it.
notes.prep: A missing side comes from the opposite sides. Keep this L-shape in mind: it comes back for area. SC1.

beats: POINT to the rectangle.
SAY: Area covers the inside, so I multiply length by width: 23 times 6.
That's tricky in my head, so I split the long side into 20 and 3.
MODEL the two parts.
SAY: 20 times 6 is 120, and 3 times 6 is 18.
I add the two parts: 138 square metres.
ASK: Use the same split.
What is the area of a rectangle 34 metres by 5 metres?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 170 m²
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 30 times 5 is 150,
and 4 times 5 is 20, so 170 square metres.
trap: multiplying only the tens.
Fix: point to the small part of the area model, and they add it.
notes.help: Draw two boxes; write each part inside.
notes.prep: Splitting a rectangle is the same move as splitting an L-shape later. SC2.

slides.title: A 6 m by 4 m garden
slides.prompt: Which one is the area? Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: adds the sides: finds the perimeter, not the area
adds one length and one width instead of multiplying

beats: SAY: Area covers the inside. Think before you point.
ASK: Which one is the area of a 6 metre by 4 metre garden?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What did A measure?
Less -> sketch the garden, trace the edge, then shade 4 rows of 6. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B, 24 square metres: 6 times 4.
A is the perimeter, and C added instead of multiplying.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: say area covers, perimeter goes around, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point: edge or inside. Every option is in m², so the unit gives nothing away. A: perimeter; C: adding once.

slides.title: Edge or inside?
slides.ask: Read the label, then solve it. Watch the unit.
slides.pivot: trace the edge or shade the inside first, then add or multiply
slides.followUp: cold call one board: How did you know to add or multiply?

items.label: A square. Perimeter?
items.say: A square has 4 equal sides: 7 four times is 28 centimetres.

items.label: Area?
items.say: Split 14: 10 times 6 is 60, and 4 times 6 is 24. That's 84.

items.label: Perimeter?
items.say: 30 metres: the missing sides are 3 and 4.

items.label: Area?
items.say: 40 times 4 is 160, and 5 times 4 is 20: 180 square centimetres.

items.label: Missing side? 7 × ? = 56
items.say: Area is length times width, so 7 times what makes 56? 8 metres.

say: Write each answer with its unit: squared for area, plain for perimeter.
trap: using the wrong measure for the label, or the wrong unit.
Fix: point to the label and the anchor, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Find the other measure for each one too.
notes.help: Copy the shape; write a number on every side or shade the inside.
notes.prep: Guided practice that mixes edge and inside. The last item works backwards: a times fact turned around. SC1 and SC2.

slides.title: Area of an L-shape
steps: Your turn: split it with a line going up.

beats: SAY: Our L-shape again: 38 centimetres around.
Area covers the inside, but an L-shape has no single length and width.
MODEL the dashed line, then each part.
SAY: So I split it into two rectangles.
The bottom is 10 by 4, which is 40.
The top is 6 by 5, which is 30. Altogether, 70 square centimetres.
ASK: Split it the other way, with a line going up. Same area?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: yes, 54 + 16 = 70
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Left part 6 by 9 is 54,
right part 4 by 4 is 16: 70 again.
trap: multiplying the two longest sides.
Fix: shade the missing corner, and they split instead.
notes.stretch: Take the corner away from a 10 by 9 rectangle instead.
notes.prep: Same shape, two measures: 38 cm around, 70 cm² inside. Split, find each area, add. SC3.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Split it into two rectangles first.
ASK: What is the area of this shape?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 81 m²
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> draw the split at 5 together, re-ask.
Still wrong -> Supported section C with me.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Bottom 12 by 5 is 60, top 7 by 3 is 21: 81 square metres.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 96, the whole 12 by 8 rectangle.
Fix: shade the missing corner, and they split it.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. After Supported section C, those students move to main Section B.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Find perimeters and areas on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Is this one the edge or the inside? How do you know?
TIME: 14 minutes. Stop everyone once at 7 minutes to share an L-shape split.
trap: adding when the question asks how much it covers.
Fix: ask edge or inside, and they choose add or multiply.
notes.stretch: Extension: the same fence making different spaces, working backwards, and a path around a pool.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: every side to label, grids to count, and L-shapes with the split drawn.
notes.prep: Independent practice across all three criteria. Most will reach the L-shapes; the sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Find the perimeter and the area of the pool.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: What are the perimeter and the area
of a pool 25 metres by 12 metres?
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 74 m and 300 m²
RECORD who swaps them, or writes m for the area.
They start the next measurement session with the teacher.
trap: writing 300 m for the perimeter, or 37 m.
Fix: none now. Record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC1 and SC2 on one new rectangle: does each student keep the two measures apart?

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how you know whether to add or multiply.

notes.answer: open - listen for edge means add the sides, inside means length times width
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can find area and perimeter?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with the two answers swapped matters most.
ASK: How do you know whether to add or multiply?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
Eyes back in 3, 2, 1.
EXPECT: around the edge means add; covering the inside means multiply
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence.
